To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cortical neuronal activity in the primary somatosensory (SI) and the secondary somatosensory cortices (SII) is strongly modulated by the vibrotactile frequency of the stimulus.
the neuronal correlates of the discrimination of vibrotactile frequencies were found in the primary somatosensory (SI) cortex and that these correlates were essential to the perception.

the neuronal activity in the primary somatosensory (S1) and secondary somatosensory cortices (S2) represents the vibrotactile stimulus features, that this representation is essential to perception, and that the neuronal representations in S1 and S2 are not independent of each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neuronal mechanisms that are responsible for sensory discrimination.
the question of which cortical neuronal activity is essential for the discrimination of vibrotactile stimulus features.
the neural mechanisms of sensory processing in the brain, in particular, the mechanisms that underlie sensory discrimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evoked activity in the somatic cortex is a necessary but not sufficient condition for perception.
perception is based on cortical neuronal representations.
the neuronal representation of the frequency difference in the primary somatosensory area S1 is essential for perception of this difference.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neuronal activity in the primary somatosensory (SI) cortex is the neural correlate for the sensory discrimination process, which is the essential process in perception.
the cortical representation of a sensory stimulus is a necessary condition for the discrimination of that stimulus.
the cortical neuronal activity is a good predictor of perceptual discrimination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cortical neurons are not only involved in sensory discrimination, but also that their responses can be used to predict the animal's perception.
a cortical neuronal representation of the stimulus features is a necessary condition for perception.
cortical neurons can encode the stimulus features and that this encoding is essential for the discrimination of the sensory stimulus.
